description: The fixture corpora `cases/` runs against. A case names one with its `corpus` key and defaults to `corpus`, so a corpus is added without touching a single existing case. `capabilities` is the part of the handshake this corpus DECIDES — not the whole block: `retrieve.vector` depends on the build and `phases`/`sangha` on whether the server reads a working git repository, and freezing those here would pin a fact about a binary onto a directory of YAML. What a corpus decides, it decides for every conforming server, and a harness asserts it after `initialize`.

corpus.why: The tree every case runs against unless it names another — a four-node `concept` graph with an installed dependency, small enough to read in one sitting and shaped so each case has exactly one thing it can fail on. `mcp/README.md` walks its nodes. Its `upstream` dependency is also what makes `dependencies` true here, and so the only corpus on which a citation can be checked against something that is actually installed.

corpus-unschematised.why: Two `gage` instances and no `.ont.yml`. It exists because `class-undeclared` is a frozen `retrieve` code that no case over `corpus/` can force a server to implement: that corpus declares `concept` and `note`, so its class set is never empty and the branch is unreachable from every case in the directory. A conforming server could answer `class-unpopulated` for an unschematised corpus — the one thing the contract says a server MUST NOT do, because it asserts an ontology the server does not have — and pass the whole suite. It is also the only corpus on which the `ontology` tier is unbacked, so it is the only one where a tool a server declines to serve is more than a hypothetical. It installs no dependency either, so it is the corpus on which BOTH optional tiers go unbacked — and `check_citation` is the tool whose unbacked behaviour is worth the most: a server that served it here could answer `external-citation-unresolved` to every citation put to it, be correct every single time, and be asserting a fact about a dependency set it does not have.

corpus-dated.why: Four `tenure` instances over an interval — a `began`, an `ended` absent while the holding is open, and one row known to the year rather than the day. It exists because NO property in `corpus/` is `type: date`, so the branch that compares two dates is unreachable from every case beside it: a server can implement no ordering operator at all, or implement one as a comparison of text, and pass the whole suite over that corpus. The shape is the one #725 measured eleven times across six real corpora, and `allen-county-ohio` states the query in its own `ACTIONS.md` over 83 instances it could not ask. What only this corpus can decide is the precision rule — `partial.yml` knows the year and not the day, so it is inside `began>=1893-06-01` on the years the two sides share and outside it as text, and a lexical implementation answers zero rows where a conforming one answers one. It installs no dependency and needs none: nothing here is about composition.
